text:
megan: Heads-up: telemetry alerted to a small but steady lift in project-less quota hits after we enabled the new Project-Affinity header feature on the router. Seeing ~8% more hits billed to org default.

devon: Which change specifically? The router started emitting `X-Project-Affinity` based on IP -> project heuristics, right?

megan: Exactly. Incoming ApiKey requests without explicit project claim now get `X-Project-Affinity` assigned by the router. But authz binder still prefers token claims and legacy headers. Some requests end up with conflicting sources and binder falls back to org.

akira: Quick note: our binder precedence is currently token_claims > standard_headers (X-Project-Id) > affinity_headers (X-Project-Affinity). If router emits affinity but no standard header, binder treats it as lower trust and in some codepaths we intentionally discard affinity for billing.

sam: Why do we discard affinity for billing? I thought it was a safety check. We added that because affinity can be noisy. But if affinity is the only signal, failing open to org causes billing delta.

megan: We need a short rollback plan + a fix candidate. Ops wants a short canary revert; product wants to keep affinity because it helps routing in many SaaS cases.

devon: Short-term: flip `router.emit_affinity=false` on infra-canary-1, and ship a compat change in authz to accept `X-Project-Affinity` as `project_id` but tag `billing_source=affinity` so we can filter. That buys time.

infra-bot: deploy queued: router-affinity-flag -> infra-canary-1 (requester=devon)

akira: Medium-term: add signal quality metrics and a confidence threshold on affinity. If confidence >= 0.9 then binder can treat it as standard header for billing; else use for routing only. Also emit `auth.affinity.confidence` metric.

megan: UX request: console currently shows only resolved project and charge. Can we add a little provenance line under the project: "resolved by: token | header | affinity" with a tooltip explaining confidence and fallback? Support will love this.

tara: I can do the console tweak. Proposal for tooltip: "This field shows which source provided the project attribution. Affinity is heuristic-based; see playbook for how confidence is computed." Add a link to internal doc.

sam: Also need telemetry: `billing.attribution.source` tag (values: token, header, affinity), `billing.attribution.confidence`. Then create a grafana panel breaking charges by source.

devon: I'll implement the compat acceptor and tag emission in authz. We should also add a fast integration test: send three requests (token-claim, X-Project-Id, inferred affinity) and assert final attribution + billing tag.

megan: Rollout plan: 1) push compat acceptor + tags to staging; 2) enable affinity in infra-canary-1 for 10% traffic with `emit_affinity=true` and `affinity_conf_threshold=0.9`; 3) monitor `billing.org_default_rate` and `billing.attribution.source` panels for 60m; 4) if stable, ramp.

console-bot: action created: TICKET-1987 (owner=tara) 1 track console provenance UI

akira: Edge case: cross-org service accounts minted by CI may have stale token claims that disagree with affinity. Binder must prefer token claims for security, but we should still surface mismatch in console: show both token_claim and affinity and highlight disagreement.

megan: Agree. Support playbook step: if provenance=affinity and token_claim exists but different, escalate to security-team for manual check. Tara, add that to the playbook.

tara: Will add. Draft playbook snippet: "If attribution=affinity and token_claim != affinity -> mark incident, contact security, collect request id and headers."

sam: Implemented metrics PR for `billing.attribution.source` and `auth.affinity.confidence`. Also added sample queries for the grafana panel.

devon: Compat acceptor merged to staging. Running integration tests now. infra-canary-1 flag flip scheduled in 10m.

infrastructure-bot: infra-canary-1 flag updated: router.emit_affinity=true (operator=devon)

megan: Monitoring: initial 15m look shows billing.org_default_rate unchanged, but we saw several attributions now tagged `source=affinity` with confidence ~0.95. Good sign.

akira: Let's keep canary for 2 hours and then increase traffic if `billing.org_default_rate` stays within 2% of baseline. Also schedule a post-rollout audit query to backfill any billing adjustments for customers affected.

megan: Thanks everyone. I'll update the RFC with the confidence threshold logic and add the console mock. We'll reconvene if the canary deviates. :thumbsup:
